title: Lavesarez 02 Pili: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Lavesarez 02 Pili: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Lavesarez 02 pili is a pili variety from Monica Genavia Turla. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Lavesarez 02 is a registered pili variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2008 as NSIC 2008 Pl 09. Monica Genavia Turla bred it. Its record notes a yield of 10,000 pcs.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Lavesarez 02 pili is grown

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [pili variety finder](/crop-varieties/pili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Lavesarez 02 was about 40 years old and about 20 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 10,000 pcs. It bears every year, with fruit in June July. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
A fruit of Lavesarez 02 weighs about 38.59 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is black. Its fruiting season is June July, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Lavesarez 02 pili

Bicol grows most of the pili. Pick a registered selection by kernel weight and the share of kernel in the nut, and plant grafted trees, because seedlings can turn out male. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Lavesarez 02?
